method.method_draft: Reflect the two secondary loads to winding 1. The resistor on winding 2 gives Z2' = (4/2)^2(10) = 40 Ω. The capacitor on winding 3 gives Z3' = (4/1)^2(-j2.5) = -j40 Ω. The input admittance is Y_in = 1/40 + 1/(-j40) = 0.025 + j0.025 S. Then I1 = V1 Y_in = 400∠0°(0.025 + j0.025) = 10 + j10 A.

method.method_draft: Find the induced secondary voltages from the turns ratio: V2 = (2/4)400 = 200 V and V3 = (1/4)400 = 100 V, using the same reference magnitude/phase as allowed by the shown common-core ideal transformer. The resistor current is I2 = 200/10 = 20 A, so its load power is S2 = 200·20 = 4000 W. The capacitor impedance is -j2.5 Ω, so I3 = 100/(-j2.5) = j40 A and S3 = 100·(j40)* = -j4000 var. Thus S_in = S2 + S3 = 4000 - j4000 VA. Since S_in = V1 I1* and V1 = 400∠0° V, I1* = (4000 - j4000)/400 = 10 - j10, hence I1 = 10 + j10 A.
